note: Made by the steps in TV_PICTURES.md: the chapter is split into sections that each carry one deep meaning ("sections"), 10 picture ideas are written for each, the top two for each picture are made and the better is chosen by eye (2026-11-22). Wide pictures only (1920x1088); the "tall" names are kept for the day tall pictures are switched back on. Each scene starts at the first word of its verse. The important part of every picture sits in the upper two thirds, clear of the words. God is not pictured; Jesus, John and Nicodemus are not portrayed as biblical people, and ordinary people of today stand in for what the verses teach.
method: Second method, asked for by Obay on 2026-11-21 after the sentence-by-sentence pictures did not connect: (1) split the chapter into sections that each carry one deep meaning, written as one plain sentence; (2) write 10 different picture ideas for each section; (3) judge them: which shows the deep meaning most truly, then which a watcher understands at once while hearing the words, then which is most engaging; (4) make the top two for each picture slot as real pictures ("candidates") and choose by eye. A section has one or two pictures.

sections.meaning: To see God's kingdom a person needs a whole new birth from above, something even a respected teacher who comes seeking at night cannot make happen by himself.
ideas: A grey-haired man in a good coat walks alone down a dark street at night toward the one lit doorway
A grey-haired man climbs an outside staircase at night toward a lit doorway at the top
A respected older man sits in his parked car at night outside a house with one lit window, hesitating
An old man stands at a hospital nursery window gazing in wonder at a row of newborn babies
A grey-haired man holds his newborn grandson and stares at him, amazed that life can start new
A butterfly breaks out of its chrysalis on a twig in light falling from above
A new green shoot springs from an old cut stump
Rain falls from above on a dry cracked field and tiny green shoots spring up
An old man studies his wrinkled face in the bathroom mirror, puzzled
A seed splits open in dark soil as light shines down on it

trials.why: beat 01a-street: both show an older man coming to a lit door at night; the street version put a stranger in the doorway, which the watcher would wonder about
beat 02b-butterfly: the old man at the nursery window shows Nicodemus's own question, how can someone be born when he is old, at once; the butterfly is beautiful but only says new life

sections.meaning: That new birth comes from the spirit: unseen like the wind, but real, and known by what it does.
ideas: A small sailboat runs fast across a bright bay, its sail full of a wind no one can see
A man stands on a grassy hilltop with his eyes closed, listening, as the wind bends the whole hill of grass
A kite climbs high on the wind while a boy holds the string
Washing on a line billows in a strong wind on a hilltop
Autumn leaves whirl up off a path in a sudden gust
Dandelion seeds are carried off into the air
A wheat field ripples in long waves under the wind
A wind chime swings on a porch with no one near it
A tall row of poplars bends all one way in the wind
A hawk hangs still on the wind above a cliff, its wings spread

trials.why: beat 03b-hill: both show an unseen wind by what it does; the boat driven over the water by a full sail is the stronger picture and shows someone carried along by the wind

sections.meaning: Only the one who came down from heaven can tell heavenly things, and he must be lifted up so that everyone who trusts him may have eternal life.
ideas: A grey-haired scholar sits late at night at a desk piled with open books, his head in his hands, baffled
An old teacher stands at his study window at night, a book forgotten in his hand, staring up at the stars
A grandfather squints, baffled, at a phone his grandson holds out to him
A man back from far away describes what he saw while his listeners shake their heads
A stranded climber on a cliff ledge reaches up as a rescuer is lowered to him on a line from a helicopter above
A man at the bottom of a deep well looks up at the bright opening as a rope comes down to him
Lost hikers in a dark valley look up at a bright flare high in the sky and turn toward it
Swimmers in a rough sea turn toward a lantern held high at the bow of a lifeboat
A crowd in a snowy night looks up to a beacon on a tall mast above the town
A man sinking in floodwater grabs a lifebuoy thrown down from a bridge

trials.why: beat 04b-stars: the scholar with his head in his hands among his books plainly shows a teacher who does not understand; the man at the starry window read as wonder, not puzzlement
beat 05b-well: the rescuer lowered from the sky to the man reaching up shows one who comes down from above to lift people up, and is the more striking picture

sections.meaning: God loved the world so much that he gave his only Son, not to condemn the world but to save it.
ideas: A father, seen from behind, stands at a tall window at dawn holding up his newborn son before a vast city waking below
A father, seen from behind, lifts his small son high in both arms on a hilltop above a wide city
The whole earth seen from space as sunlight spreads over it
A father lets go of his only son's hand on a station platform as the son leaves for a disaster zone
An old father holds his grown son's face in both hands before the son goes out into the storm
A judge steps down from his bench to help up a man who has fallen
A hand reaches down from a boat to a man in the sea
Rescue ship lights cut through a storm toward a sinking boat
A father carries his son on his shoulders through a cheering crowd
A father's hands cradle a newborn while light from a window falls on them

trials.why: beat 06a-window: the father holding his son up high before the whole city shows a father giving his son to the world; at the window he only seemed to be looking at the view

sections.meaning: The light has come; people who do wrong hide from it, and people who do the truth come gladly into it.
ideas: A man pulls the curtains shut against a bright morning and sits back in the dark lit only by a screen
A man hurriedly shoves an envelope into a drawer as the door opens and light falls across his desk
A torch beam sweeps a dark warehouse and a man ducks behind the boxes
A man in a dark alley shields his face from a car's headlights
A sunbeam falls across a room and a man moves his chair back into the shadow
A carpenter carries his finished chair out of his dim workshop into bright sunshine to look at it
A glassmaker holds a clear new vase up to a sunny window, flawless and nothing hidden
A woman throws open the shutters of her bakery so the street can see her work
A boy brings his schoolwork to his father at a sunny kitchen table
A potter lifts a finished bowl into the window light and turns it slowly

trials.why: beat 07a-curtain: the man hiding an envelope as the door opens and light falls in shows wrong works fleeing the light at once; the man at the curtains could just be someone sleeping in
beat 08a-chair: the clear vase held up in the sunlight, nothing hidden, shows work brought to the light more plainly and more beautifully

sections.meaning: John's followers are troubled that everyone is now going to the other one.
ideas: At a market, a long line forms at a new stall while two young helpers at the older stall beside it watch, worried
Two young men tug at an older craftsman's sleeve and point across the street at a crowd at another workshop
A crowd streams past a small cafe toward a new one across the square while the cafe's staff stare after them
A busker's audience drifts down the street toward another musician while his friends glare
Everyone crowds round a newly landed fishing boat while the old fisherman's sons frown
Many people walk along a river path, all heading the same way toward a bend in the river
An old ferry waits empty at its jetty while people cross a new bridge
Two lemonade stands side by side, children crowding one
Two young apprentices peer through a workshop window at a long queue across the road
A teacher's students glance over their shoulders at a bigger crowd gathering nearby

trials.why: beat 09a-stalls: the two young men pointing their calm master to the crowd across the street is the verse itself, they came to John and said everyone is going to him

sections.meaning: John is glad, like the bridegroom's friend at a wedding: the other must grow and he must become less.
ideas: At an outdoor wedding the best man stands a step back, beaming, as the groom (seen from behind) takes the bride's hands
The best man listens to the groom's vows with happy tears and a huge smile
The best man hands the groom the ring, smiling
The best man steps out of the photograph so the couple are pictured alone
The best man straightens the groom's tie before the ceremony
As the sun rises over the hills, the last bright morning star fades in the brightening sky
A man on a hillside turns down the lantern he carried through the night as sunrise floods the valley
A night watchman switches off a street lamp as the sun comes up
An old coach steps back off the pitch as the young player he trained takes the ball
The moon pales in the sky as the sun climbs

trials.why: beat 10b-vows: standing a step back beside the couple he is plainly the groom's friend, glad for him; in the close view he could be taken for the groom
beat 11a-star: the man lowering his small lantern as the sun floods the valley shows I must become less gladly; the fading star was too small to see

sections.meaning: The one from above speaks God's own words; the Father loves the Son and has given everything into his hand, and trusting him is life.
ideas: An old father's hand presses the keys of the family farm into his grown son's open hand
A father and grown son, seen from behind at a gate, the father's arm round him and his other hand sweeping out over all the land
An old craftsman hands his son his own worn tools at the workbench
A captain steps back and puts the ship's wheel into his son's hands
A father puts the reins of his horses into his son's hands
A jug of water poured into a glass that overflows and keeps on running
A view from a mountaintop above the clouds
Rain pours without measure over thirsty fields
A father stands proudly behind his son at the wheel of the family boat
An old man slips the family ring onto his son's finger

trials.why: beat 12b-gate: the keys pressed into the open hand show has given all things into his hand exactly

scenes.principle: Nicodemus, a ruler and teacher, comes to him at night.
scenes.shows: Late at night a grey-haired man in a dark coat climbs an outside stair toward a lit doorway at the top.
scenes.prompt: Late on a calm, peaceful evening in a quiet modern town, a respected grey-haired gentleman in a long dark wool coat walks up a short flight of outdoor steps toward a welcoming open doorway glowing with warm lamplight at the top. Everything else lies in soft deep-blue evening shade. He is seen from below and behind, one hand on the rail. The glowing doorway and the man are in the upper part of the picture.

scenes.principle: Unless someone is born from above he cannot see the kingdom of God. How can a man be born when he is old?
scenes.shows: An old man stands at a hospital nursery window, gazing in wonder at a row of newborn babies.
scenes.prompt: In a quiet hospital corridor, a grey-haired old man in a cardigan stands at the big glass window of a maternity nursery, one hand resting on the glass, gazing in puzzled wonder at a row of newborn babies asleep in clear cots on the other side. His face is seen in three-quarter view. Soft clean daylight. The man's face and the babies are in the upper part of the picture.

scenes.principle: Born from the spirit: the wind blows where it wants; you hear it but do not know where it comes from or goes.
scenes.shows: A small sailboat runs fast across a bright bay, its sail full of an unseen wind.
scenes.prompt: A small white sailboat heels over and runs fast across a wide bright blue bay, its sail filled full and taut by a strong wind. Ripples and whitecaps race across the water in the same direction, spray flies at the bow, and one sailor leans out at the helm. Clear midday light, white clouds driven across the sky. The boat and its sail are in the upper part of the picture.

scenes.principle: How can these things be? You are the teacher of Israel, and you do not know these things?
scenes.shows: Late at night a grey-haired scholar sits at a desk piled with open books, his head in his hands, baffled.
scenes.prompt: Late at night in a book-lined study, a grey-haired scholar in a cardigan sits at a wooden desk piled high with open books under a single lamp, his head in his hands, completely baffled. A dark window is behind him. His face, his hands and the lamp are in the upper part of the picture.

scenes.principle: No one has gone up into heaven except the one who came down from heaven; he must be lifted up, so that everyone who believes may have eternal life.
scenes.shows: A climber on a mountain ledge raises his arms as a rescuer is lowered to him on a line from a helicopter above.
scenes.prompt: A mountain rescue on a bright clear day: high on a rocky mountainside, a climber standing on a wide rock ledge raises both arms gladly toward a rescuer in a red suit who is being lowered toward him on a cable from a helicopter hovering above in the blue sky, the rescuer reaching down to him. A green valley lies far below. The climber, the rescuer and the helicopter are all in the upper part of the picture.

scenes.principle: God loved the world in this way, that he gave the only Son, so that everyone who believes in him might not perish but have eternal life.
scenes.shows: Seen from behind, a father on a hilltop lifts his small son high in both arms above a wide city.
scenes.prompt: On a grassy hilltop in clear bright morning light, seen from behind, a father lifts his small son high above his head in both arms, both of them facing a wide city spread out far below in the sunshine. The father and the lifted boy are in the upper part of the picture, against the open sky.

scenes.principle: Everyone who practices worthless things hates the light, so that his works may not be exposed.
scenes.shows: In a dim office a man shoves an envelope into a drawer as the door opens and bright light falls across his desk.
scenes.prompt: In a dim office, a man in a shirt and loosened tie hurriedly shoves a fat brown envelope into a desk drawer as the door behind him swings open and a wide bar of bright light falls across the desk and his startled face. The man, his hands and the light are in the upper part of the picture.

scenes.principle: The one who does the truth comes to the light, so that his works may be revealed.
scenes.shows: A glassmaker holds a clear new vase up to a sunny window, light passing straight through it.
scenes.prompt: In a glass workshop, a craftswoman holds a clear, newly made glass vase up to a bright sunny window, the sunlight passing straight through it and showing it flawless, nothing hidden, light sparkling on her face and hands. The vase and her face are in the upper part of the picture.

scenes.principle: Rabbi, the one who was with you is baptizing, and everyone is coming to him.
scenes.shows: Two young apprentices tug at an older craftsman's sleeve and point across the street at a crowd at another door.
scenes.prompt: On a town street on a fresh morning, two young apprentices in work aprons tug at the sleeve of an older craftsman standing calm in the doorway of his workshop, both pointing across the street, where a big crowd of people is gathering round the door of another workshop. The three men and the far crowd are in the upper part of the picture.

scenes.principle: The friend of the bridegroom stands and hears him and rejoices with joy at the bridegroom's voice.
scenes.shows: At an outdoor wedding the best man stands a step back, beaming, as the groom, seen from behind, takes the bride's hands.
scenes.prompt: At an outdoor wedding in a garden in soft afternoon light, the best man stands a step back from the couple, beaming with joy, his hands clasped. In front of him the groom, seen from behind, takes the bride's hands. The best man's glad face is the centre of the picture, in its upper part.

scenes.principle: That one must grow, but I must become less. The one who comes from above is above all.
scenes.shows: On a hillside at sunrise a man turns down the lantern he carried through the night as the sun floods the valley.
scenes.prompt: On a hillside at sunrise, a man in a coat lowers the small lantern he has carried through the night and turns down its little flame, smiling, as the rising sun floods the whole valley below with light. The man, the lantern and the sunrise are in the upper part of the picture.

scenes.principle: The Father loves the Son and has given all things into his hand.
scenes.shows: An old father's hand presses the keys of the family farm into his grown son's open hand.
scenes.prompt: A close view of an old father's weathered hand pressing a heavy ring of old keys into his grown son's open, cupped hand. Behind them, softly blurred, the wide fields and barns of the family farm in bright clear afternoon light. The two hands and the keys are in the upper part of the picture.
